top_choice_rationale: Base editing (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) is a clearly attributable new chemical capability: a deaminase tethered to a Cas9 nickase converts a single base in living cells, with the adenine editor requiring a TadA evolved to act on DNA. Products are verified at nucleotide resolution, widely reproduced, and clinically used. It is distinct from the 2020 prize, which honoured guided cleavage. Its youth and the Kondo/Nishida exclusion are real costs but do not outweigh the evidence. P004 follows as the most mature design principle, then P003 for maturity and clean attribution despite the 2010 overlap, then P002, whose six-name attribution is hard to cut to three; an award of any of these is preferred to no award.
